The shared T11 network request budget is process-local; profile-local OS file locking coalesces refreshes for the same cache path across processes, but global public quota accounting across distinct processes is not established.

The single resolver worker has a bounded caller wait and prevents per-refresh DNS thread growth, but a permanently stalled OS getaddrinfo call can occupy that worker and its accounted T11 lease until the OS call returns; later DNS requests fail closed while it is occupied.
The active host rechecks provider opt-in immediately before each scheduled fetch; cached reads remain available when approval is disabled.
A 304 renews pricing/observation timestamps only when a previously sent ETag matches; it does not renew entitlement evidence, and an unsolicited 304 does not extend freshness.
No Windows power-event callback is wired; startup checks immediately and a five-minute due-check tick observes the persisted twelve-hour deadline after the host resumes.
OpenRouter metadata refresh is disabled unless model_catalog.providers.openrouter.free_route_catalogue_enabled is explicitly true; no operational config was changed.
The 4 MiB response cap and 1,000-row cap fail closed and preserve last-good state if provider data outgrows them; automatic pagination is not implemented.
Controlled public GETs returned no ETag, so ETag/304 behavior is covered by deterministic adapter tests rather than the live probe.
